Twenty-one comments

Inion Ni Scannlain

This tune appears on Lunasa’s 2001 recording, Merry Sisters of Fate, and is written by Donogh Hennessy, who plays guitar and whistles with that band. It is, however, written in Eb major, not G major as is reported here.

Great tune!

Re: Guitar chords for Lunasa’s Inion Ni Scannlian

It’s in Eb, so maybe put capo on first fret and using D shapes
try to work out something for yourself.
Why not first start at home playing one bass note per bar to
pick out what you think might fit - and using that and the fact
that the D major can be harmonised with these chords - D,
Em, F#m, G, A, Bm, C#Dim select what chords sound right
(keep in mind that your ear should overrule theory ).

Inion Ni Scannlian, X:5

This gets played a lot in our session and I’ve always liked the tune, but needed to spend a bit of time learning it properly. I noticed that the Merry Sisters of Fate record has an interlude in the middle which wasn’t on the other settings, so I’ve added it here. Plus some chords (I play these on the accordion; they aren’t quite the same as on the record and may not be so good on guitar).

Sounds really good on the record, but it’s one of those tricky tunes which sounds slower than it really is! It has a feeling half-way between 3/4 and 6/8 which is fun to play with.

Iníon Ní Scannláin, X:7

This is the G major version of the original Eb major version by Donogh Hennessy from the Lúnasa album The Merry Sisters of Fate, with the ornamentation transcribed as faithfully as possible (identified via slowing the tune down to 50%). I’ve also added some harmonies. the grace notes without a cross line indicate a slide, the grace notes without a cross line indicate cuts, tape and bounces. I’ve also added in the staccato dot symbol where the flautist makes a break to both add emphasis and take a breath ! there is an additional slide up to the beginning G on the second time the A music is played, but the ABC notation system won’t allow an orphaned grace not at the ned of the first time bar. Does anyone know the flute that was used in this recording - was it one in Eb, but with additional low notes to get down to low Bb. If so, where does one buy such a beauty!

↳ Posted by jgm on March 9th, 2021.
